sources.entry: SwiftyMenu - Finder extension for opening selected files or folders with custom app shortcuts.

summary.name: SwiftyMenu
summary.one_liner: A macOS Finder right-click context menu tool that adds custom actions for opening files in apps, running scripts, and launching terminal commands.
use_cases: Open selected files or folders in a chosen app from Finder
Run shell or AppleScript actions on selected paths
Launch Terminal, iTerm2, or Ghostty in the current folder
Run project tasks from package.json or Makefile via right-click
Move files between Finder folders using a cut list
Start AI coding CLIs like Claude Code in a directory
summary.what_it_does: SwiftyMenu adds custom actions to the Finder right-click menu for opening selected files or folders with apps, running shell scripts, triggering AppleScripts, and running terminal commands with the selected paths passed as arguments. It supports Terminal, iTerm2, and Ghostty. Smart Commands inspect project files such as package.json, mise.toml, Makefile, Fastfile, Tuist, Podfile, and Rakefile to generate context-aware task menus. It also offers a visual cut list for moving files within Finder and an output HUD that shows command results and errors. The page states that it runs on demand, has no background daemons, and keeps all processing local.
notable: Smart Commands auto-detect project files like package.json and Makefile to build Finder menus
Built-in Terminal, iTerm2, and Ghostty launching, including AI CLI tools
Visual cut-and-move list for Finder files
Top 9 actions triggerable with number keys 1-9
caveats: In-app purchases: Lifetime Unlock $9.99, Annual $4.99, Seasonal $1.99, plus a $1.99 tip option
Page states it has not received enough ratings or reviews to display an overview
